name: First BScM class to graduate in Uganda

content.title: First BScM class to graduate in Uganda
content.summary: AKU SONAM-EA students successfully complete the registered midwife to degree midwife programme in Uganda on June 30, 2017

media.alt: First BScM class to graduate in Uganda

content.text: Being a midwife is a great privilege. Midwives help women during the most important phases of their life. A midwife's role encompasses more than just delivering babies; they are advocates for women and normal birth, and support women throughout their pregnancy and beyond. Midwives have a passion for women's health and providing the best evidencebased care.

This skilled care is especially important in lowincome countries such as Uganda. June 30, 2017 saw the first AKU SONAM-EA students successfully complete the registered midwife to degree midwife programme in Uganda. Fifteen midwives from across Uganda joined the programme in 2015.

This group has now completed the first midwifery work-study programme offered at AKU, which has enabled midwives to access higher education, while continuing to work and support their families. The low salaries earned by nurses and midwives in Uganda means that accessing university via traditional routes is virtually impossible; this unique programme opens university access to all nurses and midwives.

The programme is instrumental in developing registered midwives and giving them a platform to develop into midwifery leaders in Uganda. Generous support has been received from the Johnson & Johnson Corporate Citizenship Trust. Graduates will be crucial in helping to develop the midwifery profession and mentoring future generations of midwives.

The programme included components to help develop midwives' clinical expertise as well as their skills in critical thinking, research, evidence-based practice and leadership. During the 2.5-year programme, we also managed to increase the class size with the addition of four beautiful babies! The new mothers were supported to continue their studies and have successfully completed their BScM.
Following completion of the programme, graduates have returned to their districts where they will be able to lead and influence midwifery practice and policy development.
